_comment: EXECUTION STATUS — the honest description of what produced the record.
This file exists because an external UI review suggested renaming the
'demo-' prefix out of the record ids, reading it as sloppy naming. It is
not sloppy naming — it is true. Every published signal executed against
Bybit's demo endpoint (api-demo.bybit.com). Renaming it would have
converted a truth into a lie, so the prefix stays and this file makes the
status machine-readable so the site can state it on every page.
Update this file when the status changes, and the site follows. If real
capital is ever deployed, set simulated=false and change venue/note to
match — do NOT edit historical records, which are hash-chained.
live_path_status: built but disabled — execution requires a config/LIVE_ENABLED flag that is absent, so every live call returns 'live disabled' rather than silently trading
headline: Simulated trading record
what_is_real: The commitments. Each signal was written to the hash chain before its outcome was known, and the chain is verifiable in your browser.
The outcomes. Each close was appended when the position closed, with the price the feed reported.
The losses. Nothing is filtered. The record is currently losing money, and that is published.
The execution rules. Signals ran through the same sizing, stop and exit logic intended for live use.
what_is_not_real: The money. No real capital has been deployed. Orders were placed against Bybit's demo API, which fills against a simulated book.
The fills. A demo book can fill orders that a real, thinner book would not — particularly on small-cap pairs.
The slippage and fees. Demo execution does not reproduce real market impact or the true fee schedule, so real results would likely be worse.
The track record, as evidence of profit. It is evidence of process, not of edge.
why_published: A verified simulation is useful: it shows the method and the bookkeeping before capital is at risk, and it can be checked by anyone. It is not a claim that this would have made money.
note: Real capital is not deployed. This record is presented as evidence of process — that signals are committed before outcomes, that losses are published, and that the chain is verifiable — and not as evidence of future profit.
